NUTRITION_COMPONENT
  DESCRIPTION: Anti-inflammatory nutrition plan to support training adaptation, tissue health, and overall well-being for a desk-based, post-injury athlete.
  GOALS:
    - Reduce systemic inflammation
    - Support recovery and joint health
    - Maintain energy for training and work
    - Promote weight-neutral or modestly favorable body composition
  GUIDELINES:
    - Emphasize whole, minimally processed foods; prioritize plant-forward meals
    - Typical macro target: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight, fats 0.6–1.0 g/kg, carbohydrates remaining to fuel training
    - Protein timing: distribute 0.4–0.6 g/kg per meal across 3–4 meals; include 1–2 fast-acting protein sources post-workout if feasible
    - Anti-inflammatory staples to include daily:
      - fatty fish (salmon, mackerel) 2–3 times/week
      - olive oil as primary fat; nuts and seeds
      - colorful fruits and vegetables (berries, leafy greens, crucifers, peppers)
      - whole grains (oats, quinoa, brown rice) as tolerated
      - legumes and such for fiber and micronutrients
      - turmeric, ginger, cinnamon as flavoring; black pepper to enhance absorption
    - Pro-inflammatory triggers to limit:
      - ultra-processed foods, added sugars >10% daily calories
      - excessive saturated fat from processed meats; avoid trans fats
      - high-sodium options; limit where possible
    - Hydration: minimum 2.5–3.0 L/day; more on training days
    - Supplements (optional, discuss with clinician):
      - omega-3 fatty acids 1–2 g EPA+DHA daily (if fish intake is low)
      - vitamin D3 1000–4000 IU daily depending on 25(OH)D levels
      - a multivitamin if dietary variety is limited
  MEALS_TEMPLATE:
    - Breakfast options:
      - Greek yogurt with berries, walnuts, oats; turmeric spice
      - Omelet with spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms; whole-grain toast
    - Lunch options:
      - Grilled salmon bowl with quinoa, mixed greens, avocado, olive oil vinaigrette
      - Chicken, chickpea, and veggie whole-grain wrap; side salad
    - Dinner options:
      - Lean protein (chicken, turkey, tofu) with roasted vegetables and brown rice
      - Beef or lentil chili with beans, peppers, onions; side of greens
    - Snacks (if needed):
      - Hummus with veggies; nuts
      - cottage cheese with pineapple; apple with almond butter
  PRE/POST_WORKOUT_NUTRITION:
    - Pre-workout: balanced meal 1.5–2 hours before training or a small snack 30–60 minutes prior (e.g., banana with peanut butter; yogurt with fruit)
    - Post-workout: protein 20–40 g plus carbohydrates within 1–2 hours (e.g., protein shake with a banana, or chicken & rice)
  TRACKING:
    - Optional 2-week check-ins to monitor inflammation symptoms (joint stiffness, sleep, energy) and adjust nutrients accordingly
    - Maintain a simple food log focusing on protein intake, fruit/vegetable servings, and whole food choices
  SAFETY_NOTES:
    - If there are any gastrointestinal or allergy concerns, tailor to tolerance
    - Coordinate with medical team for vitamin D and omega-3 supplementation if needed
  IMPLEMENTATION_SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: implement anti-inflammatory nutrition guidelines from day 1
    - Phase 2: maintain guidelines; adjust macros based on progression and energy levels
  NOTES:
    - Align with overall training plan to ensure nutrition supports recovery and adaptation
    - Emphasize gradual dietary changes rather than all-at-once overhauls

CARDIO PROTOCOL
  DESCRIPTION: Cardio integration consistent with general strength plan; biweekly during Phase 1 and Phase 2, with progression to moderate volumes in Phase 3.
  SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: 2 sessions/week (as listed in weekly plan)
    - Phase 2: 2 sessions/week (as listed in weekly plan)
    - Phase 3: maintain or adjust to 2–3 sessions/week depending on recovery
  TARGETS:
    - Total weekly cardio 20–40 minutes Phase 1; 25–50 minutes Phase 2; maintain quality over quantity
  MODALITIES:
    - running, cycling, rowing as listed in weekly plans

SLEEP_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL
  DESCRIPTION: Sleep and recovery protocol to support adaptation, reduce stress, and aid recovery for a desk-based, post-injury athlete.
  GOALS:
    - Achieve sufficient nightly sleep duration
    - Improve sleep consistency and quality
    - Optimize daily recovery through structured routines
  GUIDELINES:
    - Target 7.5–9 hours of total sleep per night, consistent bed and wake times
    - Limit caffeine after noon; aim for 0–2 caffeine-containing items after 12:00 PM
    - Dim lighting 60–90 minutes before bed; minimize screens or use blue-light filter
    - Pre-sleep routine: light mobility, breathing, reading
    - Daylight exposure 10–30 minutes morning light
    - If poor sleep, consider 10–15 minute daytime nap window (early afternoon) if needed
    - Hydration: taper fluids later in the evening
  ROUTINES:
    - Sleep hygiene checklist: consistent schedule, cool/dark/quiet room, comfortable bed
    - Pre-sleep breathing: 4-7-8 or box breathing 4x4
    - Post-workout cooldown then 90–120 minutes before bed
  RECOVERY_SCHEDULE:
    - Daily:
      - Morning: 10–15 minutes light movement
      - Noon: 5–10 minutes micro-nutrition check, hydration
      - Evening: 10–15 minutes relaxation breathing or meditation
    - Training days:
      - Space intense sessions from late evening by at least 3 hours
      - Post-workout 5–10 minutes low-intensity movement and static stretching
  MONITORING:
    - Sleep duration/quality diary or app
    - Daily 0–10 recovery rating, energy, mood, soreness
    - If QoL sleep < 6 for 3+ nights, adjust bedtime earlier, reduce caffeine, refine routines
  IMPLEMENTATION_SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: implement from Day 1
    - Phase 2 & Phase 3: maintain and refine

      - whole grains (oats, quinoa, brown rice) as tolerated
      - legumes and such for fiber and micronutrients
      - turmeric, ginger, cinnamon as flavoring; black pepper to enhance absorption
    - Pro-inflammatory triggers to limit:
      - ultra-processed foods, added sugars >10% daily calories

      - high-sodium options; limit where possible
    - Hydration: minimum 2.5–3.0 L/day; more on training days
    - Supplements (optional, discuss with clinician):

NUTRITION_COMPONENT
  DESCRIPTION: Anti-inflammatory nutrition plan to support training adaptation, tissue health, and overall well-being for a desk-based, post-injury athlete.
  GOALS:
    - Reduce systemic inflammation
    - Support recovery and joint health
    - Maintain energy for training and work
    - Promote weight-neutral or modestly favorable body composition
  GUIDELINES:
    - Emphasize whole, minimally processed foods; prioritize plant-forward meals
    - Typical macro target: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight, fats 0.6–1.0 g/kg, carbohydrates remaining to fuel training
    - Protein timing: distribute 0.4–0.6 g/kg per meal across 3–4 meals; include 1–2 fast-acting protein sources post-workout if feasible
    - Anti-inflammatory staples to include daily:
      - fatty fish (salmon, mackerel) 2–3 times/week
      - olive oil as primary fat; nuts and seeds
      - colorful fruits and vegetables (berries, leafy greens, crucifers, peppers)
      - whole grains (oats, quinoa, brown rice) as tolerated
      - legumes and such for fiber and micronutrients
      - turmeric, ginger, cinnamon as flavoring; black pepper to enhance absorption
    - Pro-inflammatory triggers to limit:
      - ultra-processed foods, added sugars >10% daily calories
      - excessive saturated fat from processed meats; avoid trans fats
      - high-sodium options; limit where possible
    - Hydration: minimum 2.5–3.0 L/day; more on training days
    - Supplements (optional, discuss with clinician):
      - omega-3 fatty acids 1–2 g EPA+DHA daily (if fish intake is low)
      - vitamin D3 1000–4000 IU daily depending on 25(OH)D levels
      - a multivitamin if dietary variety is limited
  MEALS_TEMPLATE:
    - Breakfast options:
      - Greek yogurt with berries, walnuts, oats; turmeric spice
      - Omelet with spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms; whole-grain toast
    - Lunch options:
      - Grilled salmon bowl with quinoa, mixed greens, avocado, olive oil vinaigrette
      - Chicken, chickpea, and veggie whole-grain wrap; side salad
    - Dinner options:
      - Lean protein (chicken, turkey, tofu) with roasted vegetables and brown rice
      - Beef or lentil chili with beans, peppers, onions; side of greens
    - Snacks (if needed):
      - Hummus with veggies; nuts
      - cottage cheese with pineapple; apple with almond butter
  PRE/POST_WORKOUT_NUTRITION:
    - Pre-workout: balanced meal 1.5–2 hours before training or a small snack 30–60 minutes prior (e.g., banana with peanut butter; yogurt with fruit)
    - Post-workout: protein 20–40 g plus carbohydrates within 1–2 hours (e.g., protein shake with a banana, or chicken & rice)
  TRACKING:
    - Optional 2-week check-ins to monitor inflammation symptoms (joint stiffness, sleep, energy) and adjust nutrients accordingly
    - Maintain a simple food log focusing on protein intake, fruit/vegetable servings, and whole food choices
  SAFETY_NOTES:
    - If there are any gastrointestinal or allergy concerns, tailor to tolerance
    - Coordinate with medical team for vitamin D and omega-3 supplementation if needed
  IMPLEMENTATION_SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: implement anti-inflammatory nutrition guidelines from day 1
    - Phase 2: maintain guidelines; adjust macros based on progression and energy levels
  NOTES:
    - Align with overall training plan to ensure nutrition supports recovery and adaptation
    - Emphasize gradual dietary changes rather than all-at-once overhauls

      - Chicken, chickpea, and veggie whole-grain wrap; side salad
    - Dinner options:
      - Lean protein (chicken, turkey, tofu) with roasted vegetables and brown rice
      - Beef or lentil chili with beans, peppers, onions; side of greens
    - Snacks (if needed):
      - Hummus with veggies; nuts
      - cottage cheese with pineapple; apple with almond butter
  PRE/POST_WORKOUT_NUTRITION:
    - Pre-workout: balanced meal 1.5–2 hours before training or a small snack 30–60 minutes prior (e.g., banana with peanut butter; yogurt with fruit)
    - Post-workout: protein 20–40 g plus carbohydrates within 1–2 hours (e.g., protein shake with a banana, or chicken & rice)
  TRACKING:
    - Optional 2-week check-ins to monitor inflammation symptoms (joint stiffness, sleep, energy) and adjust nutrients accordingly
    - Maintain a simple food log focusing on protein intake, fruit/vegetable servings, and whole food choices
  SAFETY_NOTES:
    - If there are any gastrointestinal or allergy concerns, tailor to tolerance
    - Coordinate with medical team for vitamin D and omega-3 supplementation if needed
  IMPLEMENTATION_SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: implement anti-inflammatory nutrition guidelines from day 1
    - Phase 2: maintain guidelines; adjust macros based on progression and energy levels
  NOTES:
    - Align with overall training plan to ensure nutrition supports recovery and adaptation
    - Emphasize gradual dietary changes rather than all-at-once overhauls

CARDIO PROTOCOL
  DESCRIPTION: Cardio integration consistent with general strength plan; biweekly during Phase 1 and Phase 2, with progression to moderate volumes in Phase 3.
  SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: 2 sessions/week (as listed in weekly plan)
    - Phase 2: 2 sessions/week (as listed in weekly plan)
    - Phase 3: maintain or adjust to 2–3 sessions/week depending on recovery
  TARGETS:
    - Total weekly cardio 20–40 minutes Phase 1; 25–50 minutes Phase 2; maintain quality over quantity
  MODALITIES:
    - running, cycling, rowing as listed in weekly plans

SLEEP_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL
  DESCRIPTION: Sleep and recovery protocol to support adaptation, reduce stress, and aid recovery for a desk-based, post-injury athlete.
  GOALS:
    - Achieve sufficient nightly sleep duration
    - Improve sleep consistency and quality
    - Optimize daily recovery through structured routines
  GUIDELINES:
    - Target 7.5–9 hours of total sleep per night, consistent bed and wake times
    - Limit caffeine after noon; aim for 0–2 caffeine-containing items after 12:00 PM
    - Dim lighting 60–90 minutes before bed; minimize screens or use blue-light filter
    - Pre-sleep routine: light mobility, breathing, reading
    - Daylight exposure 10–30 minutes morning light
    - If poor sleep, consider 10–15 minute daytime nap window (early afternoon) if needed
    - Hydration: taper fluids later in the evening
  ROUTINES:
    - Sleep hygiene checklist: consistent schedule, cool/dark/quiet room, comfortable bed
    - Pre-sleep breathing: 4-7-8 or box breathing 4x4
    - Post-workout cooldown then 90–120 minutes before bed
  RECOVERY_SCHEDULE:
    - Daily:
      - Morning: 10–15 minutes light movement
      - Noon: 5–10 minutes micro-nutrition check, hydration
      - Evening: 10–15 minutes relaxation breathing or meditation
    - Training days:
      - Space intense sessions from late evening by at least 3 hours
      - Post-workout 5–10 minutes low-intensity movement and static stretching
  MONITORING:
    - Sleep duration/quality diary or app
    - Daily 0–10 recovery rating, energy, mood, soreness
    - If QoL sleep < 6 for 3+ nights, adjust bedtime earlier, reduce caffeine, refine routines
  IMPLEMENTATION_SCHEDULE:
    - Phase 1: implement from Day 1
    - Phase 2 & Phase 3: maintain and refine
